NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a two-stage ramp schedule with intermediate hold points to relax creep stress in the molybdenum rails. Standard practice uses a continuous linear ramp; this intervention introduces 30-minute holds at 600°C and 1000°C during heating to allow stress relaxation and reduce cumulative creep strain, directly mitigating the driving mechanism of hot-zone sag by interrupting the steady-state creep deformation rate.

PHYSICS CHECK — DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = cumulative creep strain; the mechanism moves it DOWN by ~15-20% (stress relaxation during holds); this REDUCES the hot-zone sag. Creep strain rate follows ε̇ = A exp(-Q/RT) σ^n; holds at intermediate temperatures reduce integrated strain by ~exp(-Q/R(1/T_hold - 1/ramp)) per hold, with n≈3-4 for molybdenum at 600-1000°C.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (all rows tagged per procurement rule)
- (a) Existing furnace controller program — modify ramp profile to include 30-minute holds at 600°C and 1000°C during heating phase
- (a) Existing temperature monitoring system — use existing thermocouples at rail locations to verify hold-point stability
- (a) Existing load-placement procedure — maintain current mass distribution during modified heating cycles
- (b) Standard programmable logic controller (PLC) timer module — configure existing timer for hold-sequence logic (stock industrial timing module)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installation: 0 new items (all parameter changes to existing controller); (a) 
- Commissioning: 1 hour programming to implement hold points in controller; (a) 
- Operation: No added labor (hold points execute automatically during heating); (a) 
- Maintenance: No additional maintenance (uses existing thermocouples); (a) 
- Operational loss: Zero (holds occur during heating ramp, not at process temperature); (a)
- Total burden: Same as standard practice (no new hardware, only software parameter change)

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Run 50 cycles with intervention vs. 50 cycles under standard practice, measure hot-zone sag via laser profilometry at each cycle end. Instruments: Existing furnace thermocouples + external laser displacement sensor (calibrated to ±0.1mm). Pass/fail: Sag reduction ≥15% in intervention group (p<0.05, t-test). Duration: 100 full furnace cycles (~6 months). Kill criterion: Sag exceeds 2mm in any cycle during test.
